answers.label: Q1
answers.solution:
The number must be (a multiple of 8, 14, 20 and 25) + 4, and the least such number uses their LCM.
\(8 = 2^3\), \(14 = 2 \times 7\), \(20 = 2^2 \times 5\), \(25 = 5^2\)
LCM \(= 2^3 \times 5^2 \times 7 = 8 \times 25 \times 7 = 1400\)
Required number \(= 1400 + 4 = 1404\)
Check: \(1404 = 8 \times 175 + 4 = 14 \times 100 + 4 = 20 \times 70 + 4 = 25 \times 56 + 4\).
So, the least number is 1404.

answers.label: Q2
answers.solution:
Let the cost price be \(C\).
Selling price at a gain of 5% \(= 1.05C\)
Selling price at a loss of 5% \(= 0.95C\)
The difference is the reduction: \(1.05C - 0.95C = 0.10C = 50\)
So \(C = \frac{50}{0.10} = 500\) dollars.
Original selling price \(= 1.05 \times 500 = 525\) dollars.
So, the original selling price is 525 dollars.

answers.solution:
Note: as printed the question cannot be solved. Dividing by \(\frac{4}{5}\) is the same as multiplying by \(\frac{5}{4}\), so Tanmaya's answer would equal the correct answer, not be 36 more. The sensible reading is that he was asked to multiply by \(\frac{4}{5}\) and instead divided by \(\frac{4}{5}\).
Let the number be \(x\).
Correct answer \(= \frac{4}{5}x\)
His answer \(= x \div \frac{4}{5} = \frac{5}{4}x\)
\(\frac{5}{4}x - \frac{4}{5}x = 36\)
\(\frac{25x - 16x}{20} = 36\)
\(\frac{9x}{20} = 36\)
\(x = \frac{36 \times 20}{9} = 80\)
Check: \(\frac{5}{4} \times 80 = 100\), \(\frac{4}{5} \times 80 = 64\), difference 36.
So, the given number is 80.

Profit = SP of 33 m - CP of 33 m.
Given: Profit = SP of 11 m.
So CP of 33 m = SP of 33 m - SP of 11 m = SP of 22 m.
Profit % \(= \frac{\text{Profit}}{\text{CP}} \times 100 = \frac{\text{SP of 11 m}}{\text{SP of 22 m}} \times 100 = \frac{11}{22} \times 100 = 50\%\)
So, the profit percentage is 50%.

Exterior angle of the first polygon \(= 180^\circ - 144^\circ = 36^\circ\)
Number of sides \(= \frac{360^\circ}{36^\circ} = 10\)
The second polygon has \(2 \times 10 = 20\) sides.
Its exterior angle \(= \frac{360^\circ}{20} = 18^\circ\)
Its interior angle \(= 180^\circ - 18^\circ = 162^\circ\)
So, each interior angle of the second polygon is \(162^\circ\).

answers.solution:
Side of the square \(= \sqrt{16} = 4\) cm.
The midpoints are 2 cm from each corner, so each side of the inner square is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 2 cm and 2 cm:
Side \(= \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{8}\) cm
Area of inner square \(= (\sqrt{8})^2 = 8\) cm\(^2\)
(Equivalently, the four corner triangles each have area \(\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 2 = 2\), so the inner square is \(16 - 4 \times 2 = 8\).)
So, the area is 8 cm\(^2\), half the original square.

answers.solution:
Note: as printed, \(12x^2 - 17xy + 26y^2\) has no factors: we need two numbers with product \(12 \times 26 = 312\) and sum \(-17\), and none exist (\(17^2 - 4 \times 312 < 0\)). The intended term is almost certainly \(6y^2\), so we factorise \(12x^2 - 17xy + 6y^2\).
Product \(12 \times 6 = 72\), sum \(-17\): the numbers are \(-9\) and \(-8\).
\(12x^2 - 17xy + 6y^2 = 12x^2 - 9xy - 8xy + 6y^2\)
\(= 3x(4x - 3y) - 2y(4x - 3y)\)
\(= (3x - 2y)(4x - 3y)\)
So, the answer is \((3x - 2y)(4x - 3y)\).

\(2\pi r = 40\pi\)

So, the radius of the new circle is 20 cm.

In triangle PRQ, \(\angle R = 40^\circ\) and \(\angle Q = 40^\circ\).
\(\angle P = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - 40^\circ = 100^\circ\)
ST is parallel to PR, and PS (part of PQ) is a transversal.
Angle x (\(\angle PST\)) and \(\angle RPS\) are co-interior angles, so they add up to \(180^\circ\):
\(x = 180^\circ - 100^\circ = 80^\circ\)
(Check: \(\angle QST = \angle QPR = 100^\circ\) as corresponding angles, and \(x + 100^\circ = 180^\circ\) on the straight line PQ.)
So, \(x = 80^\circ\).

Distance walked \(= \frac{18}{25}\) of the perimeter \(= \frac{18}{25} \times 5 = 3.6\) sides.

answers.label: Q15
answers.solution:
The four large circles of radius \(r\) touch each other in pairs, so their centres form a square of side \(2r\).
Diagonal of this square \(= 2r\sqrt{2}\).
The small circle sits at the centre of the square, so the distance from its centre to the centre of any large circle is half the diagonal \(= r\sqrt{2}\).
The small circle touches each large circle, so this distance = \(r +\) (radius of small circle).
Radius of small circle \(= r\sqrt{2} - r = r(\sqrt{2} - 1)\) (about \(0.414r\)).
So, the radius of the inner circle is \(r(\sqrt{2} - 1)\).

answers.solution:
The father's share is 3 times the share of each other member.
Father's share \(= \frac{1}{4}\), so each other member gets \(\frac{1}{4} \div 3 = \frac{1}{12}\) of the cake.
Cake left for the others \(= 1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}\)
Number of other members \(= \frac{3}{4} \div \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3}{4} \times 12 = 9\)
Total members \(= 9 + 1 = 10\)
So, there are 10 members in the family.

\((x + y)\) is common to all three terms:
\((a+b)(x+y) + (2a+3)(x+y) - (3a+4b)(x+y)\)
\(= (x + y)[(a + b) + (2a + 3) - (3a + 4b)]\)
\(= (x + y)[a + b + 2a + 3 - 3a - 4b]\)
\(= (x + y)(3 - 3b)\)
\(= 3(x + y)(1 - b)\)
So, the expression factorises as \(3(x + y)(1 - b)\).

Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add up to \(180^\circ\).
Let them be \(2x\) and \(3x\): \(2x + 3x = 180^\circ\), so \(5x = 180^\circ\) and \(x = 36^\circ\).
The angles are \(2 \times 36^\circ = 72^\circ\) and \(3 \times 36^\circ = 108^\circ\).
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
So, the four angles are \(72^\circ, 108^\circ, 72^\circ, 108^\circ\).

The largest four digit number is 9999.
Divide 9999 by 459: \(459 \times 21 = 9639\) and \(459 \times 22 = 10098\) (five digits).
So \(9999 = 459 \times 21 + 360\); the remainder is 360.
Required number \(= 9999 - 360 = 9639\)
So, the largest four digit number divisible by 459 is 9639.

Let the sum be \(P\). Then SI \(= \frac{3}{8}P\) and \(R = \frac{25}{4}\%\).
\(\text{SI} = \frac{P \times R \times T}{100}\)
\(\frac{3}{8}P = \frac{P \times \frac{25}{4} \times T}{100}\)
\(\frac{3}{8} = \frac{25T}{400} = \frac{T}{16}\)
\(T = \frac{3}{8} \times 16 = 6\)
So, the time is 6 years.

answers.solution:
Remove the innermost bracket (the bar) first: \(\overline{2x - y}\).
\(3x - (2x - y) = 3x - 2x + y = x + y\)
So \(3(3x - \overline{2x - y}) = 3(x + y) = 3x + 3y\)
Also \(2(3x - 2y) = 6x - 4y\)
Now the curly bracket:
\(\{4y - (6x - 4y) - (3x + 3y)\} = 4y - 6x + 4y - 3x - 3y = 5y - 9x\)
Now the square bracket:
\([15y - (5y - 9x)] = 15y - 5y + 9x = 10y + 9x\)
Finally:
\(23x - (9x + 10y) = 14x - 10y\)
So, the expression simplifies to \(14x - 10y\).

answers.label: Q23
answers.solution:
(a) Note: the exponents as printed, \((m+k)\) on the second factor and \((k+n)\) on the third, do not give a fixed value (the product would be \(x^{(m-n)(m+n-2k)}\)). The standard question has exponents \((m+n)\), \((n+k)\) and \((k+m)\), each the sum of the two indices inside its bracket, and that is solved here.
\(\left(\frac{x^m}{x^n}\right)^{m+n} = x^{(m-n)(m+n)} = x^{m^2 - n^2}\)
\(\left(\frac{x^n}{x^k}\right)^{n+k} = x^{(n-k)(n+k)} = x^{n^2 - k^2}\)
\(\left(\frac{x^k}{x^m}\right)^{k+m} = x^{(k-m)(k+m)} = x^{k^2 - m^2}\)
Product \(= x^{m^2 - n^2 + n^2 - k^2 + k^2 - m^2} = x^0 = 1\)

(b) \(\frac{1}{1 + x^{n-m}} = \frac{1}{1 + \frac{x^n}{x^m}} = \frac{x^m}{x^m + x^n}\)
\(\frac{1}{1 + x^{m-n}} = \frac{1}{1 + \frac{x^m}{x^n}} = \frac{x^n}{x^n + x^m}\)
Sum \(= \frac{x^n + x^m}{x^m + x^n} = 1\)

So, (a) = 1 and (b) = 1.

Let the first part be ₹ \(x\); the second part is ₹ \((1200 - x)\).
SI on first part \(= \frac{x \times 6 \times 2}{100} = \frac{12x}{100}\)
SI on second part \(= \frac{(1200 - x) \times 8 \times 3}{100} = \frac{24(1200 - x)}{100}\)
These are equal:
\(12x = 24(1200 - x)\)
\(x = 2(1200 - x) = 2400 - 2x\)
\(3x = 2400\), so \(x = 800\)
Second part \(= 1200 - 800 = 400\)
Check: SI on 800 \(= 800 \times 0.12 = 96\); SI on 400 \(= 400 \times 0.24 = 96\).
So, the two parts are ₹ 800 and ₹ 400.

First three-fourth of the journey \(= \frac{3}{4} \times 360 = 270\) km
Time for it at 60 km/hr \(= \frac{270}{60} = 4\frac{1}{2}\) hours
Remaining distance \(= 360 - 270 = 90\) km
Remaining time \(= 5\frac{3}{4} - 4\frac{1}{2} = 1\frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{4}\) hours
Speed \(= 90 \div \frac{5}{4} = 90 \times \frac{4}{5} = 72\) km/hr
So, the speed for the rest of the journey is 72 km/hr.

answers.label: Q27
answers.finalAnswer: 60; 60; Hindi; Science; Mathematics and Social Science
answers.solution:
Note: the pie chart prints Social Science as \(5^\circ\), but the angles of a pie chart must add up to \(360^\circ\). The other four are \(90^\circ + 55^\circ + 70^\circ + 80^\circ = 295^\circ\), so Social Science must be \(360^\circ - 295^\circ = 65^\circ\) (the drawn sector also looks about that size). We use \(65^\circ\).
Marks for a subject \(= \frac{\text{angle}}{360^\circ} \times 540 = \text{angle} \times 1.5\)
Mathematics \(= 90 \times 1.5 = 135\)
English \(= 55 \times 1.5 = 82.5\)
Hindi \(= 70 \times 1.5 = 105\)
Science \(= 80 \times 1.5 = 120\)
Social Science \(= 65 \times 1.5 = 97.5\)
(i) English + Science + Social Science \(= 82.5 + 120 + 97.5 = 300\); Hindi + Mathematics \(= 105 + 135 = 240\). Excess \(= 300 - 240 = 60\) marks.
(ii) Hindi + Mathematics \(= 240\); English + Social Science \(= 82.5 + 97.5 = 180\). Excess \(= 240 - 180 = 60\) marks.
(iii) 105 marks were scored in Hindi.
(iv) \(22.2\%\) of \(360^\circ \approx 80^\circ\) (and \(\frac{120}{540} \times 100 = 22.2\%\)), so the subject is Science.
(v) English and Science differ by \(80^\circ - 55^\circ = 25^\circ\), i.e. 37.5 marks. Mathematics and Social Science also differ by \(90^\circ - 65^\circ = 25^\circ\) (135 - 97.5 = 37.5 marks).
So, the answers are: (i) 60, (ii) 60, (iii) Hindi, (iv) Science, (v) Mathematics and Social Science.

\(\frac{90}{100}M = 540\), so \(M = \frac{540 \times 100}{90} = 600\)
Without a discount he would sell at ₹ 600 and make a 20% profit:

answers.label: Q30
answers.solution:
The figure shows three parallel lines (all slanting the same way) cut by two transversals: one falling to the right, one rising gently to the right.
On the right parallel line, the angle between the line (upward) and the rising transversal (to the right) is \(70^\circ\). On the left parallel line, the angle between the line (upward) and the falling transversal (to the right) is \(112^\circ\).
a: at the middle parallel line, a is in the same position as the \(70^\circ\) angle (corresponding angles), so \(a = 70^\circ\).
b: b lies on the same straight transversal next to a (a linear pair), so \(b = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ\).
d: at the left parallel line, d is vertically opposite the angle corresponding to \(70^\circ\), so \(d = 70^\circ\).
e: at the right parallel line, e is in the same position as the \(112^\circ\) angle (corresponding angles), so \(e = 112^\circ\).
c: c and e form a linear pair on the falling transversal, so \(c = 180^\circ - 112^\circ = 68^\circ\).
So, \(a = 70^\circ\), \(b = 110^\circ\), \(c = 68^\circ\), \(d = 70^\circ\), \(e = 112^\circ\).
